body: Large language models (LLMs) are used as post hoc explainers of sequential decision-making policies, producing natural-language explanations of why an action was chosen. However, LLMs often generate plausible but incorrect statements, and no existing approach systematically tests whether such explanations are faithful to the underlying environment. Two classic software testing challenges stand in the way: there is no oracle for the correctness of an explanation, and the test inputs, natural language queries about a policy's behavior, lack the structure needed for systematic test case generation. We address both. Probabilistic model checking provides the test oracle, computing exact reference results against which LLM answers are graded automatically. A taxonomy of post hoc query categories structures the input space around the environment-level facts from which policy explanations are composed; test cases generated from it are prioritized by question-specific diagnostic difficulty scores. Across seven MDP environments, the testing separates three open-weight LLMs: a reasoning model passes 85% of test cases, a mid-size model 70%, and a 1B model falls below the random baseline, while prioritization surfaces significantly harder cases than random selection. Our results indicate how trustworthy LLM-generated explanations are in model-free settings, where the same LLMs are used but no oracle exists to verify them.
summaryZh: 大语言模型常被用作序列决策策略的事后解释器，但其生成的解释往往缺乏环境忠实度且缺乏自动化评估准则。本文提出使用概率模型检测作为测试基准（Oracle），并通过事后查询类别分类构建测试输入空间，根据诊断难度进行优先级排序。对三个开源大模型在七个马尔可夫决策过程（MDP）环境中的测试表明，推理型模型表现较好，而小模型表现低于随机基准，揭示了无模型设置下LLM解释的可信度边界。

glossary.explanationZh: 事后解释器，指事后对模型决策过程进行自然语言解释的工具或大模型
概率模型检测，通过严密数学计算生成准确参考结果以验证系统行为的形式化方法
测试预言机/判定准则，用于判断测试输出是否正确的基准系统
序列决策策略，强化学习或控制系统中随时间连续选择动作的策略模型
